To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fully automated method for the diagnosis of supraventricular arrhythmias using surface electrocardiogram was developed, and that it was evaluated in a study that included 68 patients (42 for validation) and achieved average sensitivity of 83%, average specificity of 96%, and average accuracy of over 93%.
a fully automated method for supraventricular arrhythmias (SVAs) classification was proposed, based on atrial waves detection and a clinically based tree.
the proposed method for automatic classification of SVT in the ECG achieves an average accuracy of 0.93 (95% CI, 0.92 to 0.94) and an average sensitivity of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.86).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an algorithm for SVT classification in the surface ECG.
the development of an automatic method for the classification of SVTs using a hidden AEA-wave detection method and a clinically based tree.
the classification of SVTs using surface ECG.

the presented method is a valuable and accurate decision support tool for the detection of SVTs, which may be used in a clinical environment.
the proposed method may serve as an accurate, fast, and reliable decision support tool, which may allow the detection of SVTs with high accuracy using noninvasive methods.
the presented method may be used as a valuable decision tool in the clinical practice, allowing accurate detection and classification of SVT using noninvasive methods.
